hints.content: In order to find $G'(2)$, we should first find an expression for $G'(x)$ (for any input $x$) in terms of $f$, $g$, and their derivatives.

So $G'(x)=\dfrac{f'(x)g(x)-f(x)g'(x)}{[g(x)]^2}$.

We can now plug $x=2$ into this expression:

$G'(2)=\dfrac{f'(2)g(2)-f(2)g'(2)}{[g(2)]^2}$

We are given that $f(2)=-4$ and $f'(2)=4$.

Since $g(x)=2x^2$, we know that $g(2)=8$ and $g'(2)=8$. [[☃ explanation 1]]

Let's plug in those values!

$\begin{align}
G'(2)&=\dfrac{(4)(8)-(-4)(8)}{(8)^2}
\\\\
&=\dfrac{64}{64}
\\\\
&=1
\end{align}$

\\\\\\\\

\\\\\\\\

\\\\\\
&=4x
\end{align}$

### Finding $g'(2)$

>$\begin{align}
g'(\blueD{2})&=4(\blueD{2})
\\\\\\\\
&=8
\end{align}$
